messages:
Nora: Heads-up — us-west-2 GPU fleet provisioning failing since 03:12 UTC. Many CreateInstance/Attach volumes are erroring with 403s, warm pool not filling.
Priya: I see the same. API errors show AccessDenied on KMS decrypt for kms-key/redwood-models and a bunch of outbound denies from firewall-rule-ccp.
Ben: That firewall tighten was merged in infra-firewall#423 to restrict outbound to unapproved endpoints pending SOC review. Snippet from the ACL: ```hcl
# egress deny (intentional)
rule { cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0" action = "deny" description = "block external kms endpoints" }
```
Ben: We inadvertently blocked the regional KMS endpoints used by our model storage which are considered "external" in the new rule.
oncall-net: Confirmed: rule firewall-rule-ccp matched traffic to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com -> DENY. Policy change was propagated to border proxies at 03:08.
AuditBot: Alert: 1200 denied KMS decrypt attempts in 5m for role:arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-node-role (rule=firewall-rule-ccp).
Nora: Because decrypts are failing, the model-fetcher falls back to slower cross-account rewrap flow which spawns lots of short-lived connections to our external keystore (spikes NAT and conntrack). Warm pool stalled at 7/50.
Priya: Two quick options: 1) revert deploy of infra-firewall#423, or 2) add allowlist entries for kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com and s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com for gpu-subnet service CIDRs. Revert is fastest.
Ben: Revert needs SOC ack but oncall-net can hotfix an allowlist for only the kms and s3 endpoints used by model loads. I'll raise a revert PR as backup.
oncall-net: I'll push an allowlist change for the two endpoints and roll proxies. Change: permit egress to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com and s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com for tag:Service=gpu-warm. Rolling now.
AuditBot: Notice: firewall-rule-ccp patched (allow kms/s3 for gpu-warm) by oncall-net runbook-allow-01.
Priya: After the patch we're seeing KMS decrypt success and S3 GET 200s. Warm pool rising: 22/50 ready (was 7/50).
Nora: Follow-ups: 1) narrow the allowlist to specific kms key ARNs instead of wildcard endpoints, 2) add an integration test that simulates model warm path with tightened firewall in staging, 3) cost and audit note for increased cross-account keystore calls while we were failing.
Ben: Filing SEC-issue-7712 to track SOC approval for the final policy and INFRA-5011 for the integration test.
Nora: Good. Monitoring for 60m. If we see >5% model fetch errors, escalate to network + infra.
